- Fixed attribute access in debug flag check by using `.value` for 'buildtype' option to align with option value retrieval pattern.

Support custom install permissions for targets and files

Add support for specifying custom file permissions during installation using the `install_mode` keyword argument. This applies to build targets, custom targets, headers, man pages, data, and subdirectories. The specified mode is now preserved during installation instead of defaulting to standard permissions.

Move option merging and setting logic to CoreData

The merge and set operations for user and other options are now centralized in the CoreData class. This removes duplicated logic from Environment and Conf classes and ensures consistent behavior when handling option values. The change simplifies maintenance and reduces code duplication across components that process build options.

Rename clike to clink for clarity and accuracy

The term "clike" is misleading as it suggests C-like syntax, but the code actually refers to languages that can be linked with C. Renamed clike_langs to clink_langs, sort_clike to sort_clink, and related variables to better reflect their purpose of determining linker compatibility rather than syntax similarity.

Use anonymous name for empty dependency names in logs

When a dependency has an empty or missing name, use '(anonymous)' in log messages instead of an empty string to improve clarity and avoid confusion in output.

Replace raw log calls with deprecation function

Use a dedicated `mlog.deprecation()` function for all deprecation warnings instead of manually formatting them with `mlog.log` and `mlog.red`. This standardizes the output and simplifies future changes to deprecation message formatting.

Simplify cross-build system checks using get_host_system

Introduce get_host_system method to safely retrieve the host system name and use it across platform checks. This reduces code duplication and improves readability by centralizing access to the host machine system value.

Use compiler tests to determine valid C++ standard flags

Instead of relying on version comparisons, test whether the compiler accepts specific -std= arguments. This makes C++ standard flag selection more reliable across different compiler versions and platforms, especially for Clang and GCC with non-standard versioning.

Replace compiler type constants with CompilerType enum

- Introduce CompilerType enum to replace scattered integer constants for GCC, Clang, and ICC compiler types
- Add helper properties (is_standard_compiler, is_osx_compiler, is_windows_compiler) to simplify platform checks
- Update all compiler classes and detection logic to use the new enum instead of raw integers
- Replace direct comparisons with type checks using the new properties for better readability and maintainability

Refactor command-line argument parsing into a central class

Move argument parsing logic into a dedicated CommandLineParser class in mesonmain.py to unify handling of subcommands. Each subcommand module now provides add_arguments() and run() functions, eliminating duplicated argument parsing and improving code organization. This change simplifies adding new subcommands and ensures consistent behavior across all commands.

Set up MSVC environment in Visual Studio project files

Use vcvarsall.bat or VsDevCmd.bat to configure the MSVC environment when generating Visual Studio project files. This ensures the correct compiler architecture settings are applied during builds. Also fix target platform name in error message and improve Windows architecture detection when using MSVC 2017.

Extract LLVM tool name variants into reusable function

The logic for generating versioned names of LLVM-related tools (like llvm-config and scan-build) is now centralized into a shared function `get_llvm_tool_names`. This eliminates duplication and ensures consistent ordering and naming across dependencies.

Move git subprocess logic to mesonlib for reuse

Introduce a centralized `git` function in mesonlib to handle Git subprocess calls consistently across the codebase. This includes proper handling of console input/output, especially on Windows where Git can interfere with ANSI color support. The function is now used by both msubprojects and wrap modules, eliminating duplication and ensuring uniform behavior when interacting with Git repositories.

Initialize test result with success and add step failures incrementally

The TestResult class now starts in a successful state and accumulates output and timing data per build step. Failures are set explicitly via a new fail() method when issues occur during configuration, build, test, install, or clean phases. Each step's output and duration are appended incrementally, improving clarity and maintainability of test result tracking.

Define test protocols as an enum

Introduce a TestProtocol enum to represent test output protocols (exitcode and TAP) instead of using raw strings. This improves type safety and centralizes protocol handling, with helper methods to convert from strings and to string representation. The change updates related code to use the enum.

Delete wrap-redirect files during purge

When purging subprojects, wrap-redirect files are now properly deleted. The change adds tracking of the original filename and redirection state, ensuring that both the redirected wrap file and its target are cleaned up when requested. Tests are updated to verify the deletion of redirect files.

Allow saving intermediate embeddings during optimization

The `n_epochs` parameter now accepts a list of integers to specify epochs at which intermediate embeddings are saved. The optimization runs for the maximum epoch in the list and returns all requested embeddings in increasing epoch order. These are stored in `aux_data["embedding_list"]` and exposed as `embedding_list` in the UMAP estimator.

Update unique victory conditions for France, Mughals, and America

- France now needs to build the Louvre and Metropolitain instead of the Statue of Liberty for its third goal
- Mughals now need to build Shalimar Gardens instead of Harmandir Sahib for their second goal
- America's second goal expanded to include Brooklyn Bridge and Golden Gate Bridge in addition to existing wonders

Add support for configurable AWS regions in S3 driver

- Introduced a region-to-host mapping to support multiple AWS regions
- Enhanced error message with bucket and used region details
- Added region validation and dynamic host selection in S3 driver
- Provided a method to list all supported regions

Move utility functions into setup.py to avoid dependencies

To ensure setup.py can run without external dependencies, key utility functions (get_packages, get_data_files, and related helpers) have been inlined directly into setup.py. These were previously imported from libcloud.utils.dist, which depends on libraries not available during initial installation. This change allows the package to be built and installed in clean environments.

Add support for partial object downloads via byte range

New methods `download_object_range` and `download_object_range_as_stream` are introduced to allow downloading a specific byte range of a storage object. The existing `_save_object` method is updated to accept a `partial_download` flag to skip size validation for partial content. Drivers for local storage and S3 implement the new functionality using range requests.

Add support for partial content downloads in storage drivers

- Added PARTIAL_CONTENT to AzureResponse valid status codes for range requests
- Introduced _get_standard_range_str in base storage driver for standard Range header formatting
- Implemented download_object_range and download_object_range_as_stream in Azure Blobs driver
- Updated S3 driver to use the new standard range string method

Add timeout support to script deployment and execution

Introduce an optional timeout parameter for ScriptDeployment and ScriptFileDeployment classes, allowing users to specify a maximum runtime for script execution. The timeout is passed through to the SSH client's run method, which has been updated to accept the same parameter. Tests have been extended to validate timeout functionality and ensure backward compatibility.

Use namespace-ignoring XML find functions in AWS responses

Some AWS responses include namespaces while others don't, causing potential parsing failures. Introduced `findtext_ignore_namespace` and `findall_ignore_namespace` to first try parsing with the expected namespace, then fall back to no namespace if needed. Updated AWS response handling to use these resilient functions.

Add test coverage for all OpenStack auth versions

Introduces a new test class to validate that the OpenStack driver can be instantiated with all supported authentication versions, including 2.0, 3.x, and OIDC-based tokens. Uses a composite mock HTTP class to route requests appropriately per version.

Support file aliases and standard input in graph management

- Added support for file aliases to allow multiple names for the same imported graph
- Enabled handling of standard input (stdin) as a valid data source for graph imports
- Improved file path normalization and identity checking to support aliases and stdin
- Updated graph import logic to preserve metadata when reusing or renaming graphs
- Enhanced file info management to support alias-based lookups and updates

Enable CONCAT function support in Kypher queries

The `CONCAT` function is now supported in Kypher queries by translating it to SQLite's `||` operator during SQL conversion. This allows users to use `CONCAT` in their queries as per Cypher syntax, which is then properly handled by the underlying SQLite engine.

Handle virtual graphs in query translation

Adds support for virtual graphs in KGTK queries by integrating with SqlFunction for translation and execution. Virtual tables are now properly recognized during clause processing, and index creation is skipped for them to prevent errors. A new vtable registry in TranslationState tracks active virtual tables and their implementations.

Add support for disabling query optimization

Introduces a `dont_optimize` flag to prevent automatic sorting of graph joins, preserving the original clause order in SQL generation. This allows users to control join order for performance or correctness in complex queries where optimizer-driven reordering may be undesirable.

Rename ref_geom parameter to geom in multiple classes and functions

The parameter `ref_geom` has been renamed to `geom` across several modules to improve consistency and clarity in naming. This change affects JFactory, map-making functions, exposure, background, PSF map, and related tests. The functionality remains unchanged.

Ensure unique names for datasets and models

- Default name is now set to None, generating a unique name automatically using a UUID
- Added checks to ensure all dataset and model names are unique, replacing duplicates with auto-generated names
- Updated copy methods to optionally accept a new name, defaulting to a generated one
- Import order adjusted in several files to match standard conventions

Enable selective application of PSF and energy dispersion

Add support for controlling PSF and energy dispersion application per model via a new `processing` attribute. Models now include a `processing` dictionary that determines whether PSF and edisp are applied during prediction. This allows finer control over the simulation or fitting process, especially for models where these effects should be skipped. The change updates model initialization, I/O, and evaluation logic to respect these settings.

Update model tag checks for list support

Model tags are now defined as lists to support multiple aliases. Adjust comparisons to check membership instead of direct equality. Update tag access in serialization and registry to use the first list element as primary identifier.

Add option to simplify model serialization output

Introduce a `full_output` parameter to `to_dict` and related methods to control the verbosity of serialized model representations. When `full_output=False`, parameter attributes (min, max, frozen, error) are omitted if they match the default values defined in the model class. This results in cleaner, more readable YAML output for basic use cases while preserving full fidelity when needed.

Add piecewise broken power-law spectral model

Introduces a new spectral model that defines a piecewise broken power-law with fixed energy nodes and user-defined flux values at those nodes. The model uses linear interpolation in log-log space between nodes and supports serialization to and from dictionaries. Unit handling and parameter validation are included.

Add support for configurable comment markers in header and data sections

Previously, only "#" was treated as a comment marker and could not be customized. The parameter has been renamed from `ignore_comments` to `ignore_data_comments` in data section functions to clarify its scope, and now accepts a tuple of strings to define custom comment markers. Header section comments can now be controlled via the `ignore_comments` argument in `lasio.read()` and `lasio.examples.open()`.

Stop audio processing gracefully on shutdown

Adds proper shutdown handling to stop audio threads and prevent resource leaks. The change introduces a stop mechanism in the recognizer and producer components, ensuring clean termination of audio processing loops. It also adds runtime configuration reloading when changes are detected.

Add support for one-time event handlers

Introduce a `once` parameter to `add_event` to allow event handlers that automatically unregister after being triggered once. This change updates internal event tracking and modifies scheduling to use one-time registration when appropriate. Tests confirm the handler runs once and is removed.

Simplify intent registration and remove global lists

Replaces global lists for tracking decorated intent handlers with direct attribute storage on functions. This allows the skill to discover and register intents by inspecting method attributes during initialization, eliminating the need for shared state. The `need_self` parameter is removed as it is no longer required.

Use alphanumeric skill IDs instead of numeric mappings

- Replace `to_letters` function with `to_alnum` to convert skill IDs to alphanumeric strings, allowing non-numeric IDs and preserving underscores
- Update all skill ID handling to work with string-based IDs instead of integers
- Adjust tests to use string skill ID 'A' instead of numeric 0
- Remove integer casting of skill IDs in intent service and skill manager

Add audio seek forward and backward functionality

New message bus events for seeking audio forward and backward are implemented, allowing skills and services to skip or rewind playback by a specified number of seconds. Backend support is added in the VlcService, and corresponding methods are exposed in the skill-facing AudioService.

Simplify skill settings synchronization logic

Removed redundant device-to-device settings sync and hash tracking. Now always uses skill_gid to request and upload settings, reducing complexity and state management. The skill settings are now directly fetched using the skill's global identifier without checking other devices.

Use modern Python syntax for ABC base classes

Replace legacy `__metaclass__` attribute with `metaclass` keyword argument in class definitions across audio, STT, and TTS modules to align with Python 3 syntax.

Deprecate intent_file_handler and improve intent registration

The intent_file_handler decorator is now deprecated in favor of using intent_handler, which can handle both intent objects and intent files. A new internal method _register_adapt_intent is introduced to streamline intent registration, and intent file support is integrated directly into register_intent. Tests are updated to verify intent file registration through both the old and new methods.

Load and process test cases in skill integration tests

Introduces helper functions to load test case files and handle various input types such as utterances, play queries, and questions. Refactors test execution logic into smaller methods for better readability and maintenance. Adds dedicated methods to manage skill contexts, simulate user responses, and evaluate test results. Improves timeout handling and queue processing during test execution.

Split speech into chunks with end-of-utterance listening control

The `expect_response` flag is now handled at the chunk level when speaking. Only the final chunk triggers listening, allowing Mycroft to wait for a response only after the full message is spoken. This improves interaction flow by preventing premature activation of the microphone during multi-sentence responses.

Free disk space in cache when thresholds are exceeded

Adds helper functions to convert MB to bytes and manage cache cleanup by removing oldest files first. The cache curation now triggers only when both minimum free disk space and percentage thresholds are breached, improving reliability of disk space management.

Add support for tracking and removing wrapped fallback handlers

Introduces a wrapper map to track original and wrapped fallback handlers, enabling proper removal by either reference. Updates registration and removal logic to handle wrappers correctly and improves feedback on removal success or failure.

Add MessageWaiter class for waiting on messages

Introduces a new MessageWaiter class that simplifies waiting for specific message types on the message bus. It allows setting up a wait condition, performing actions, and then blocking until the message arrives or a timeout occurs. The existing wait_for_response method is updated to use this class, reducing code duplication and improving maintainability. A new wait_for_message method is also added to the MessageBusClient for direct use of this functionality.

Track skill process lifecycle with status updates

Introduce a ProcessStatus class to manage and report the lifecycle state of the skills process. It replaces ad-hoc status methods in SkillManager with a centralized state tracker that emits messagebus events, triggers callbacks, and supports queries for is_alive and ready states. This improves consistency and enables better external monitoring.

Add support for configurable FFmpeg DLL names on Windows

Introduces a new configuration option `ffmpeg_libs_win` to specify custom FFmpeg DLL filenames on Windows, allowing version-specific naming. The loader now searches for matching DLLs based on prefixes defined in this option, falling back to generic names if needed.

Implement audio and video packet queues with dynamic refill

Adds dedicated audio and video packet queues with bounded sizes to manage playback and seeking efficiently. Introduces a refill mechanism that asynchronously fills queues when they are low, ensuring smooth playback and fast seeks by preloading packets. Audio and video packets are now processed and stored separately with proper timestamp handling.

Replace worker thread with pyglet clock for audio buffering

The audio player no longer uses a dedicated worker thread to refill buffers. Instead, it schedules periodic checks using pyglet's clock to refill audio data when needed. This simplifies thread management by removing the lock and worker thread dependency, relying on pyglet's event loop for timing.

Fix on_eos event for audio-only sources with silent driver

Schedule on_eos event when playing audio-only sources if no audio driver is available, ensuring the event is dispatched after the source duration. This handles cases where audio playback is silent or unavailable.

Update BQL syntax for setting variable stattypes

Changes the BQL syntax from `MODEL col AS type` and `GUESS stattypes FOR` to `SET STATTYPES OF col TO type` and `GUESS stattypes OF`. This change applies consistently across population schema definitions and updates the parser and test cases accordingly.

Implement conditional mutual information with constraint support

Adds proper handling of constraints in column_mutual_information by supporting both fixed and marginalized conditions. When constraints contain null values, the method now performs marginalization via sampling, otherwise applies constraints directly. Introduces helper methods to format and simulate constraint rows in the format required by the Loom backend.

Clear antimony state before conversions and improve error handling

- Ensure antimony's internal state is reset before each conversion by calling `clearPreviousLoads()` in all conversion functions to prevent interference from prior operations.
- Fix incorrect use of identity comparison (`is`) with string literal in `distributed_sensitivity_analysis`, now using equality comparison (`==`).
- Remove unused `sys` import.
- Improve error handling in `extractFileFromCombineArchive` by removing unused variable assignment.

Remove unused import and add error handling for optional dependency

- Removed `sbml2matlab` from startup imports as it is not used
- Made `phrasedml` import optional with try/except blocks to handle missing dependency
- Improved error reporting when SED-ML conversion fails by including the original exception message
- Cleaned up redundant code paths related to working directory handling

Extend wallet_send.py test to support descriptors

Adds descriptor wallet support to wallet_send.py by importing descriptors directly using a fixed xpriv/xpub pair. For legacy wallets, maintains backward compatibility with importmulti, while descriptor wallets use importdescriptors with ranged imports. Adjusts wallet setup and funding logic to handle differences in how descriptor and legacy wallets manage keypool and watch-only behavior.

Enable profiling only during specific scheduler operations

Introduces a profiling context manager to selectively enable profiling in scheduler methods. Profiling is now scoped to the relevant code blocks using a context manager, replacing manual enable/disable calls. A `nullcontext` backport is added for consistent context management when profiling is disabled.

Use RegressionManager factory for test discovery

Introduces a classmethod `from_discovery` on RegressionManager that handles test and hook discovery internally. Discovery logic is now separated into static methods `_discover_tests` and `_discover_hooks`, improving modularity. The main RegressionManager constructor now requires explicit test and hook lists, promoting clearer initialization. Logging is centralized using a module-level logger.

Add task identification and coroutine stack introspection

Introduces unique task IDs for better debugging and enhances task representation with detailed coroutine stack introspection. Tasks now display their execution state, current coroutine, and trigger in `repr`, improving debug visibility. Utility functions to walk and extract coroutine stack traces are added to support this feature.

Improve binary resolution performance and clarity

Replace string-based character replacement with a translation table using `str.translate()`, which is more efficient and cleaner. Introduce a `_ResolveTable` class to handle resolution of ambiguous bits (like 'x', 'z') based on environment settings, supporting error, zero, one, or random resolution modes. This change simplifies the logic and improves maintainability.

Use descriptive operation constants for datastore actions

Replaces the generic TxnActions constants with a new Operations class that uses more readable string values ('put', 'delete') for datastore mutations. This improves code clarity by making the intent of each operation immediately obvious. All related code and tests are updated to use the new constants.

Move utility functions to shared module

The functions for generating Celery queue names, task annotations, and worker module names are moved from `tq_config.py` to `utils.py` to improve code organization and reusability. They are now imported where needed instead of being defined in the configuration class.

Add Monit integration with status monitoring and control

Introduces a MonitOperator class to interact with Monit's HTTP API for process management. Adds support for checking process status, sending commands (like start/stop), waiting for desired states, and ensuring processes are running. Includes a cooldown mechanism for reload operations to prevent excessive calls. Status values are standardized using a new MonitStates enum.

Use KazooClient instance instead of host string in DeploymentConfig

Passing a pre-configured KazooClient instance allows for better control over ZooKeeper connection settings and improves consistency across components. The change updates all callers to create and manage the KazooClient instance before passing it to DeploymentConfig.

Ensure watches are restarted and handle project deletion

Previously, when a project or configuration section was deleted, the associated ZooKeeper watch could remain active unnecessarily. This change adds proper tracking of watch states and ensures watches are restarted when needed. It also prevents further updates when the watched entity no longer exists, by checking project/section existence before processing updates. This avoids lingering watches and ensures consistent state after deletions.

Ensure counter meets minimum value and support ID reservation

Adds functionality to ensure ID counters do not fall below a specified minimum, both for sequential and scattered allocators. Introduces caching to reduce unnecessary database requests when checking reserved values. Expands the datastore API to support reserving specific IDs, preventing their reallocation, and adds handling for datastore_v4 AllocateIds requests.

Return empty string for error responses in datastore

Previously, an empty protocol buffer was encoded and returned even when errors occurred, which could lead to unnecessary serialization. Now, an empty string is returned instead of an encoded empty response for all error cases, while maintaining the same error code and message. This change applies consistently across transaction, query, mutation, and administrative operations.

Use EntityLock for grooming index entries

Replaces manual ZooKeeper lock acquisition and release with the EntityLock context manager when deleting stale index entries. Adds a helper to derive entity group keys from table keys for locking. This simplifies lock handling and reduces the risk of leaving locks dangling.

Support external API server for specific services

Adds support for routing certain API calls, like app_identity_service, to an external API server. This is configured via a new `external_api_server` parameter in `ConfigureRemoteApi` and related functions, and can be specified through the `--external_api_port` command-line flag in devappserver2. The change allows mixed deployments where some APIs are handled locally and others are delegated externally.

Track entity groups involved in transactions

Adds support for associating entity groups with transactions by storing the group references in ZooKeeper under the transaction's path. This allows better tracking and management of which entity groups are involved in a transaction, improving consistency and aiding in debugging and monitoring of transactional operations.

Use persistent ZooKeeper locks for entity groups

Replaces ephemeral ZooKeeper locks with persistent ones to prevent lock release on connection loss. Locks are now explicitly acquired and released, improving reliability during transient issues. Timeout errors are standardized using a new TimeoutError exception.

Remove unused imports and simplify transaction rollback

- Removed unused imports (threading, api_base_pb) to clean up dependencies.
- Simplified rollback_transaction by removing unnecessary protocol buffer decoding since the transaction ID is now passed directly.
- Improved error handling by raising InternalError directly instead of returning error codes.
- Aligned caller code to pass transaction ID instead of full request, reducing overhead and improving clarity.

Add support for updating datastore indexes

Introduces a new handler to process datastore index updates via the `/api/datastore/index/add` endpoint. The change includes models for representing indexes and their properties, validation logic, and storage management using ZooKeeper. Indexes are merged with existing ones, avoiding duplicates based on a composite identifier.

Replace ring parsing with gossip-based node information

The script now uses `nodetool gossipinfo` instead of `nodetool ring` to gather node state, load, and token information. This change simplifies parsing and improves reliability by leveraging gossip data that includes explicit node status and load values. A new `--skip-tokens-check` flag allows bypassing the single-token validation, and `--skip-ownership-check` allows skipping the ownership validation, making the tool more flexible for different cluster configurations.

Enforce unique ports in HAProxy configuration and improve version routing cleanup

Introduces validation to ensure no two app versions use the same port in HAProxy, raising an error if duplicates are detected. Enhances cleanup by properly stopping version routing and removing stale entries when versions are deleted or lack required configuration.

Move transaction commit logic to request handler

The commit transaction logic has been moved from the DatastoreDistributed class to the MainHandler class. The functionality remains the same, but the handling of transaction commits is now centralized in the request handler, reducing redundancy and improving code organization. The unit test for the removed method has also been deleted since the logic is now tested indirectly through the handler.

Use custom service account for GCS operations in backups

Adds support for specifying a custom service account when performing datastore backups to Google Cloud Storage. The account, if provided, is passed through to all GCS interactions including validation, file writing, and bucket access checks. A new input field is added to the backup configuration form to allow specifying the service account name.

Implement service account and access token support

Adds support for service account-based authentication using JWT assertions and access tokens. The AppIdentityService now retrieves service account keys from ZooKeeper, generates signed assertions, and exchanges them for OAuth2 access tokens. The PrivateKey class is updated to generate proper JWT assertions with correct headers and metadata, and to support loading keys from PEM data. Access tokens are returned with expiration times for proper lifecycle management.

Use custom service accounts for GCS operations

- Moved service account fetching logic to utils module
- Added support for specifying service accounts in backup/restore operations
- Updated UI forms to include service account selection
- Modified GCS access functions to use specified service accounts
- Adjusted request handlers to pass service account information through the workflow

Add support for __property__ metadata queries

Enables querying indexed property types per kind by introducing a new PropertyIterator. This allows listing all properties of a kind along with their supported types (e.g., INT64, STRING) by scanning index metadata. The change includes helper constants for int64 type boundaries and handles __property__ queries in the index manager.

Use consistent output directory structure for plots and files

Files are now saved in organized subdirectories under the output directory. A new `fname_with_default_dir` function ensures consistent path handling, replacing the old `get_abspath`. Plot and data files for different benchmarks are saved under group-specific subdirectories to avoid naming conflicts and improve output organization.

Refactor ABI checker to use version objects

Introduce RepoVersion class to encapsulate revision details for old and new versions, improving code organization and reducing parameter lists. The ABI checker now takes these version objects instead of individual revision and repository parameters, making the interface clearer and more maintainable.

Improve metadata combination script with better error handling and origin tracking

- Enhanced argument parsing description to clarify behavior when merging metadata from multiple sources.
- Added input validation with descriptive error messages to ensure matching numbers of metadata files and origins.
- Track strains per origin to enable accurate one-hot encoding of origin columns.
- Set origin flags ("yes"/"no") for all strains across all origins, not just those present in each file.
- Improved code clarity and robustness during merge process.

Add functions to parse column renaming rules and strip prefixes

- Introduced `parse_new_column_names` to process renaming rules in the format "old=new" and return a dictionary mapping old to new column names, with validation and warnings for invalid formats.
- Added `strip_prefixes` to remove specified prefixes from strain names using regex, improving reusability and clarity.
- Refactored the main script to use these functions, replacing inline logic for column renaming and prefix stripping with cleaner, modular calls.

Enable using '.' to select items under current directory

The '.' notation is now supported to select tests, plans, and stories located under the current working directory. When used, it automatically resolves to the correct relative path within the metadata tree. Documentation and command help have been updated to reflect this new shorthand.

Use updatable progress messages with colored states

Use context manager for HTTP sessions with retries and timeout

Remove unused 'keys' parameter from wake() method

This change simplifies the method signature and aligns subclasses with updated base behavior.

Log trial creation and improve Ax search resumption

Update preprocessing script and dataset loading for simplified CLI and config

- Enhanced preprocessing output with detailed counts and progress messages

Handle unsupported combine modes via fallback

Instead of raising an error for unsupported combine modes, delegate to the parent class's score_emb method to allow fallback handling. Adds support for 's*o' combination in RelationalScorer and corresponding score_so method in KgeModel to compute scores for subject-object pairs against all or specified relations. Disables score_so in ReciprocalRelationsModel since it cannot score relations.

Use underscores instead of asterisks in combine modes

Replaces asterisks (*) with underscores (_) in combine mode identifiers across all scorers and documentation, such as "sp*" becoming "sp_" and "*po" becoming "_po". This change affects how scoring modes are specified in training, evaluation, and model-specific logic.

Use param instead of selection in filter predicates

Enables proper composition of selection parameters using logical operators (~, &, |) by introducing SelectionPredicateComposition. This ensures that parameter references are correctly expressed as {"param": "name"} in the output JSON, aligning with the expected Vega-Lite schema.

Add support for grouping nodes in distribute function

Enables the `distribute()` function to partition MPI nodes into isolated groups, allowing nested parallelization where each group can independently execute distributed tasks. This is controlled via the new `group_nodes` parameter, which supports equal or unequal group sizes. Results from grouped executions cannot be returned to a single node.

Add support for parallel execution via job splitting

Introduce --jobid and --njobs command-line options to split experiments across multiple parallel runs. The system now distributes experiments deterministically so that each job processes a unique subset, enabling efficient parallelization from a single YAML script. Experiments are assigned in a round-robin fashion based on job ID and total number of jobs.

Move module imports into functions for faster CLI startup

This change relocates module imports from the global scope into individual functions across multiple command modules. This reduces initial import overhead, resulting in faster command-line interface startup times.

Optimize path hint generation with reusable logic state

Initialize a shared Logic instance for path hint calculations to avoid redundant setup. Save its initial state and reuse it across calls by resetting before each simulation, improving performance and consistency.

Simplify call_module by managing session internally

The function now automatically creates and destroys a GMT C API session, removing the need for users to manually pass a session object. This change simplifies usage and aligns with GMT's command-line behavior.

Start global modern mode session on import

Initializes a global GMT modern mode session when the module is imported, ensuring that modern mode is active by default. The session is managed through a new `GMTSession` class that automatically cleans up temporary files when the session ends. This change removes the need for users to manually call `begin` and `end` in basic workflows.

Start global GMT session at import and clean up at exit

Replaces the `GMTSession` class with direct calls to `begin` and `end`. The global modern mode session now starts when the package is imported and automatically ends when Python exits, ensuring proper cleanup without relying on object destruction.
API call failed

Wait for block counts using waitFor instead of sync_with_ping

Add a new `sync_getdata` method to TestNode to wait for specific getdata requests, and replace multiple `sync_with_ping` calls with `waitFor` checks on block height for more precise synchronization. This improves test reliability by waiting for actual expected conditions rather than assuming progress after a ping.

Add minValue parameter to nonNegativeDerivative and perSecond

The minValue parameter allows handling counter resets or wraps that go below a specified threshold, similar to how maxValue handles upper bounds. When a value drops below minValue, it is treated as a counter wrap, and the delta is calculated accordingly. This change updates both nonNegativeDerivative and perSecond functions, along with their internal logic and test cases.

Use consistent authentication headers across all requests

Introduces a unified method for setting authentication headers, replacing the previous `_getHassioHeaders` with `_getAuthHeaders` that uses `Authorization: Bearer` for most requests. Adds support for `X-Supervisor-Token` header via `_altAuthHeaders` for specific cases like authentication. Updates all request methods to use the new header methods and allows custom headers in `_postHassioData`. The simulated supervisor now accepts both header formats for compatibility.

Replace custom comparison and formatting with jsoncomparison

The script now uses the `jsoncomparison` library to handle JSON comparison instead of custom logic, improving reliability and maintainability. The verbose output option has been added to display the full JSON and diff during execution. Custom pretty-printing is removed in favor of standard `json.dumps` with consistent formatting.

Disable hash checking in HTTP fetch by default

Adds an optional parameter to skip hash verification when fetching HTTP content. This is useful for test environments where the hash check is unnecessary and can be safely bypassed. All test mocks are updated to accommodate the new parameter signature.

Remove binascii dependency from hash handling

The `get_hash` function now returns bytes directly after unhexlifying the downloaded checksum, and validation ensures the checksum has the expected length for the given algorithm. Callers no longer need to unhexlify the result themselves, centralizing and simplifying hash handling.

Warn if desktop Qt is missing for mobile targets

When installing Qt for Android or iOS, the desktop version of Qt is required as a dependency. This change adds a warning if the desktop Qt is not installed, informing the user how to install it. Additionally, an `--autodesktop` flag is introduced to automatically install the required desktop Qt version without manual intervention.

Enable testing with simulated GCE routing

Adds support for simulating GCE instance routing in multi-host tests, where each host has a /32 IP and relies on a router for connectivity. This includes setting up appropriate IP addressing, routing, and enabling IP-in-IP tunneling for cross-host communication. The test now runs twice for "rules.tags": once without simulation and once with GCE-like routing enabled.

Enable testing via PR comments containing [test]

Adds support for triggering tests through pull request comments that contain the phrase [test]. The system now listens for 'created' and 'edited' webhook events, checks if the comment is on a pull request, verifies the presence of [test] in the comment body, and confirms the commenter is in the admin whitelist before triggering tests.

Update PR status during testing and improve payload handling

The pipeline now actively updates the pull request status on GitHub with "pending" or "failure" states during test execution. It extracts pull request title and body to avoid JSON parsing issues, passes structured data to the test script, and handles webhook responses more robustly. The test script has been updated to expect separate environment variables for title and body, and relies on the pipeline for PR status updates instead of managing them itself.
API call failed

Ensure garbage collection runs before and after tests

Adds garbage collection hooks to test functions to stabilize memory usage during testing, particularly in non-CI environments. This helps prevent spurious failures due to unpredictable GC timing, especially in memory-intensive tests.
API call failed

Set OpenROAD tool defaults from PDK

Removes hardcoded OpenROAD variable defaults from the tool setup and instead reads them from the PDK configuration. If a default is not defined in the PDK, the variable becomes a requirement that must be set by the user. This change centralizes technology-specific parameters in the PDK files for better maintainability and consistency.

Move docstring trimming utility to shared module

The `trim` function, used to clean up docstring indentation for proper RST parsing, has been moved from `dynamicgen.py` to `utils.py` and is now reused across multiple modules. This avoids code duplication and centralizes a common utility for consistent formatting in documentation generation.

Convert Python values to safe TCL syntax

Add proper escaping and type conversion when writing values to TCL format, ensuring special characters, environment variables, lists, tuples, and booleans are correctly handled. This prevents TCL parsing errors when sourcing the generated manifest.
API call failed

Update log checking to track errors and warnings metrics

The check_logfile method now returns a dictionary with match counts per regex suffix. When 'errors' or 'warnings' suffixes are defined, their match counts are automatically stored in the corresponding metrics for the task. The report files are now saved in the current directory using '<design>.<suffix>' naming. Documentation and examples have been updated to reflect the new behavior and highlight the special handling of 'errors' and 'warnings' suffixes.

Update error and warning metrics incrementally and improve tool setup

The error and warning counts from log files are now added to existing metrics instead of overwriting them, ensuring accurate accumulation across runs. Tool setup logic has been centralized into a dedicated `_setup_tool` method, which also automatically registers log files in the tool's report configuration when regex patterns for errors or warnings are defined. Documentation has been updated to reflect that metrics are accumulated and log files are auto-included in reports.

Support array inputs and fix band/channel ordering in cutout requests

Extends input validation to accept numpy arrays for 'band' and 'channel' parameters. Ensures correct ordering of band and channel ranges in the request payload by swapping values when necessary. Updates documentation with a 3D cutout example using frequency range.

Validate query parameters before sending request

Adds validation of query parameters against a known list of allowed parameters for the SVO FPS service. Raises `InvalidQueryError` with a descriptive message if invalid parameters are provided. Removes a redundant test that relied on a low-level VOTable parsing error, replacing it with tests that verify the new validation logic.

Simplify dummy response setup by removing unused parameters

Default values are now used for context, body, and headers in set_data calls, reducing redundancy in test setups. This change applies to multiple test files and makes the test code cleaner and easier to read without altering behavior.

Use column attributes fixture for Gaia query result validation

Adds a shared fixture with expected column attributes and uses it to validate query results instead of repeating individual checks. This simplifies test code and ensures consistent validation across multiple test methods.

Use shared test fixtures and modern path handling

Replaces repeated test setup code with reusable pytest fixtures (`mock_querier` and `mock_querier_async`) that encapsulate common test dependencies. Uses `pathlib.Path` for robust and readable file path resolution. Simplifies individual test methods by injecting preconfigured test objects, reducing duplication and improving maintainability.

Convert TestTap class to standalone test functions

The test suite previously used a class-based structure for organizing tests. It has been refactored to use standalone functions instead, removing the TestTap class wrapper while preserving all test logic and functionality. This change aligns with current testing practices and improves readability.

Use standard urlencode function directly

Previously, multiple classes defined their own `url_encode` method that wrapped `urllib.parse.urlencode`. This led to redundant code and indirection. The change removes these custom methods and uses `urllib.parse.urlencode` directly wherever URL encoding is needed. This simplifies the codebase and reduces maintenance overhead.

Use pathlib for reading test data files

Replaces custom file path handling and `utils.read_file_content` with `pathlib.Path` for reading test data. Pre-loads test data into module-level constants where possible to simplify repeated file reads. Removes the deprecated `read_file_content` utility function.

gain type annotations, automagic conversion from/to YAML, no need for
explicit moves of fields between instances and serialized data.

Reboot has to check for boot time

Previous attempt with closing connection was not succesful as shown by
/tests/execute/reboot/reuse_provision

btime in /proc/stat is boot time in seconds since epoch and reboot()
will make sure that it has changed

Adds disk requirement for tests/full which is helps with testing

Remove unused keys parameter from wake() methods

This seems to be no longer used, and makes `wake()` more complicated
than necessary.

Unify Polarion case searching

Save and load ids to/from results.yaml.
Add constant for extra identification keys.
Raise ReportError on TC not found in Polarion.

Replace blank "type: ignore" with more specific waivers

Using mypy's error codes, waivers can target the actual erorr, leaving
space for other kind of violations to not be suppressed.

Add a helper for importing a member from a module

This primitive appeared twice already, and follows the same
scenario: import a module, then locate a member (a class, usually)
in the module, and catch possible errors along the way.

Document & correct use of class conversion methods

Recently added `{to,from}_{serialized,raw,dict}` methods for various
conversions were poorly documented, and sometimes even wrongly used.
This patch adds a short summary on when to use them, and fixes some
sub par bits around the code.

Drop various guest `wake()` methods in favor of parent class

They all do the same things anyway: instantiate a guest class, with
given data, pass parent and name down the stream. A base class can do
all of this.

Fix resuming of SOBOL generator during ax search

This is done by fixing the seed and regenerating trials already performed.

Support for dataset-specific configurations and metadata

preprocess now creates a dataset.yaml file with information about
the dataset.

Add support for relation prediction

Added a score_so method to KgeModel for this purpose and a default
implementation in RelationalScorer (which is currently used by all models).

Rename queries sp*/s*o/*po to sp_/s_o/_po

This makes them valid identifiers, which allows to use query types as
configuration keys (for example).

Define SelectionPredicateComposition

Made a new class SelectionPredicateComposition to allow use of ~,&,| with certain PredicateCompositions.  Rewrote test_filter_transform_selection_predicates to match the new syntax.

Add MPI parallelization on different MPI communicators.

This is necessary to parallelize functions that are also parallelized.

Add jobid and njobs argument to script command.

This allows to run multiple experiments from the same script in several parallel executions of YANK.

Move CLI imports into functions for speed

In order to prevent the CLI from taking long times due to importing everything, especially when the user mis-types a command for docopt to handle, import statements for the CLI functions have been moved to the actual functions instead of the module header

Improve performance of path hint generation

Avoid instantiating tons of different logic instances and just reuse the same instance by resetting its state every time it's needed.

Create and destroy C sessions inside call_module

Removes the need to always do this when using the C API. It's what the
command line app does anyway so it's not wasteful.

Hide away session management

Implement a GMTSession class to handle calling begin and end. Use it as
a global (package level) session. This way, each script/notebook uses
a single session. begin and end are no longer public API functions.

Replace the global GMTSession with 'atexit'

No need for the class or the global instance. Register 'end' with
'atexit' to make sure end is called when exiting Python.

Add 4 block attack scenarios to PV python testing

Also add the needed option -pvtest which slows down the checking
of inputs by putting a sleep time of 1 second for each input to
check.  This allows up to simulate very long to validate blocks
used in the attack scenarios.

Improve reliablility of p2p-acceptblock.py

Numerous timing issues do with the the multi-threading and also
the requestmanager. Better to no rely on sync_with_ping() and also
we have to handle getheaders requests and subsequent multi hash
getdata requests.

Add a minValue option to nonNegativeDerivative and perSecond

It works in a way similar to maxValue: when the counter wraps, instead of
producing a null value, it computes the difference assuming the counter wrapped
to minValue.

Use alternate headers for HA auth requests

When sending a "Authorization: Bearer" header to the supervisor's /auth endpoint, the header gets used to authorize the addon and then _also_ authorize against HA which fails.  This changes requests made to the /auth enpoint so they use the "X-Supervisor-Token" header to avoid the conflict.

Use library instead of ad-hoc code

This replaces `pretty_print_combos` with `json.dumps`, and
`compare_combos` with `jsoncomparison.Compare`.

Allow `MetadataFactory.fetch_http` to skip sha256

`MetadataFactory.fetch_http` must often download HTML pages, not
Updates.xml files. download.qt.io does not store checksums for these
files, so this particular function must be allowed to download these
pages without using a checksum.

Fix implementation of `helper.get_hash`

Causes `get_hash` to verify the hash length, and check that the hash can
be unhexlified properly.

Fixes the interface for `get_hash` so that the caller does not have to
run `binascii.unhexlify` or verify its output.

Add CLI option to install desktop qt automatically

This change also causes aqt to emit a warning when the option is not
turned on and the expected desktop Qt is not found.

Add test to simulate GCE instance setup

This change adds a test that sets up hosts' addressing and routing as it
is on a GCE instance, and checks that we still get connectivity between
workloads on different hosts.

Allow tests to be run on demand

With this change, a string "[test]" can be added as a comment to a pull
request by a whitelisted user to initiate testing on a pull request

Refactor to update pull requests with pending status

This commit refactors code to update the pull request with a pending
status at the earliest possible time.

Additionally, this refactor includes fixes an issue where unexpected
characters in the pull request title or body caused issues parsing
github webhook payload json

Check for available memory instead of its total amount in tests

This change prevents the python interpreter from triggering the
OOM-killer while trying to use/allocate more memory than available on
the system.

Reduce pressure on memory in stream tests

This change runs the python garbage collector before and after each
stream test.

The garbage collector is disabled in the CI since it has a significant
impact on the duration of the jobs (which are time constrained in the CI).

Fix multiline strings in schema examples

Using '\' or multiline strings results in extra whitespace, so it seems
best to use Python's automatic concatenation of adjacent strings.

Remove PDK-specific var defaults from openroad.py

We shouldn't be hardcoding tech-specific values in tool setup scripts,
so we should use the new ['pdk', 'variable'] parameter to drive these.

In order to support user overrides, we'll still drive them through the
['eda', ... 'variable'] keypath in the TCL script.

Fix RST parsing in schemagen

- Use Python standardized docstring "trim" function to preserve newlines
  and indentation in schelp strings.
- Fix schemagen parse_rst() to handle multiline text

Make _print_tcl() more robust

- Use {} to escape strings, so that we can have spaces and newlines
- Dump tuples as lists to avoid parsing
- Make sure envvar syntax gets subbed in anywhere in string

Tweak string escape approach

Use "" instead of {} to remove persistent backslashes in front of curly
braces in string.

Make tool regex set errors/warnings metrics

- "errors" and "warnings" suffix is special case
- Also update docs for relevant schema param and check_logfile()

Make regex errors/warnings additive, add reports

- Enables tools to extract additional errors/warnings from other logs
- Add logfiles under reports to reduce boilerplate, the logfiles always
  belong if regex is used

Add a spectral cutout example

Also include support for numpy arrays for band and channel, and autocorrect the band and channel values to be in ascending order

Validate `svo_fps` query parameter names locally

`SvoFpsClass.data_from_svo()` now checks the names of the query
parameters and only connects with the server if all names are valid.

Simplify setting DummyResponse data in TAP+ tests

`DummyResponse` is used in `esa/jwst` and `gaia` tests for mimicking
server responses. Now the response data can be specified by only setting
the parameters that have non-default values.

Simplify column attribute checking in `gaia` tests

The function `__check_results_column()` tested if the attributes (e.g.
description) of the columns of the query results match the expectation.
This function is now replaced with
`astropy.table.BaseColumn.attrs_equal()`, and the comparison data is now
provided by a `pytest` fixture.

Reduce duplication in setting up `gaia` tests

The new module level fixtures allowed removing setup code from many
tests.

Remove `TestTap` class from `gaia` tests

Grouping the tests together in a test class served no purpose and
eliminating the class removed a level of indentation.

Remove `utils.tap.conn.TapConn.url_encode()`

The removed method simply called the standard library
`urllib.parse.urlencode()`.

Remove an utility function for reading test data

`astroquery.utils.tap.xmlparser.utils.read_file_content()` has been
replaced with the standard library `pathlib.Path.read_text()`.
Furthermore, in the modules where multiple test functions previously
used `read_file_content()` to read the data files, they are now read
once at the module level instead.

references:
Support CUDA stream on memory pool

Now, memory pool will have an arena (bins) for each stream
to avoid concurrent streams touch the same memory block

Complete overhaul of filter testing.

These tests are much more flexible now for when additional filters are added.

Use "import numpy as np" in the array_api submodule

This avoids importing everything inside the individual functions, but still is
preferred over importing the functions used explicitly, as most of them clash
with the wrapper function names.

Use _implementation on all functions that have it in the array API submodule

That way they only work on actual ndarray inputs, not array-like, which is
more inline with the spec.

Use better type signatures in the array API module

This includes returning custom dataclasses for finfo and iinfo that only
contain the properties required by the array API specification.

Make the array API left and right shift do type promotion

The spec previously said it should return the type of the left argument, but
this was changed to do type promotion to be consistent with all the other
elementwise functions/operators.

Implement the array API result_type() manually

np.result_type() has too many behaviors that we want to avoid in the array API
namespace, like value-based casting and unwanted type promotions. Instead, we
implement the exact type promotion table from the spec.

Fix for orphaned items that may develop from a failed watcher event.

- Also added optional (but on by default) silencing of verbose and useless botocore logs.

Add options to post metrics to queue

This commit adds an option to SM to post metrics to cloudwatch.
Metric data will be posted whenever scan queue items are added or
removed.

Use named field for command_template when generating ninja command.

The command template become easier to read with named field.

Rewrite custom_target template string substitution

Factor it out into a function in mesonlib.py. This will allow us to
reuse it for generators and for configure_file(). The latter doesn't
implement this at all right now.

Also includes unit tests.

Use the same function for detection of C and C++ compilers

The mechanism is identical which means there's a high likelihood of
unintended divergence. In fact, a slight divergence was already there.

Use an enum instead of strings for method names.

If a non-string value is passed as a method, reject this explicitly
with a clear error message rather than trying to match with it and
failing.

Add 'Compiler.get_display_language'

Use this when we print language-related information to the console and
via the Ninja backend.

Add ConfigToolDependency class

This class is meant abstract away some of the tedium of writing a config
tool wrapper dependency, and allow these instances to share some basic
code that they all need.

Enable searching system crossfile locations on more platforms

There's no reason not to also look in these places on Cygwin or OSX.  Don't
do this on Windows, as these paths aren't meaningful there.

Move test_cross_file_system_paths from LinuxlikeTests to AllPlatformTests.

Use include_directories for D impdirs.

Change the code to store D properties as plain data. Only convert them
to compiler flags in the backend. This also means we can fully parse D
arguments without needing to know the compiler being used.

Use test setups from the active (sub)project by default.

Replace the logic where a test setup with no project specifier defaults to
the main project with one that takes the test setup from the same
(sub)project from where the to-be-executed test has been read from.

Create a helper for checking if a string has a path component

This is used in a number of places, and in some places it is incomplete.
Use a helper to ensure it's used properly.

Fix b_ndebug=if-release option

Provide get_{type}_options_for_target() methods that unite {type} and builtin options.

Add macOS linker versioning information

This patch exploits the information residing in ltversion to set the
-compatibility_version and -current_version flags that are passed to the
linker on macOS.

Add 'install_mode' to all installable targets

This makes it possible to customize permissions of all installable
targets, such as executable(), libraries, man pages, header files and
custom or generated targets.

This is useful, for instance, to install setuid/setgid binaries, which
was hard to accomplish without access to this attribute.

Move to coredata some methods handling options

Those methods only use coredata object, so better just move them as a
coredata method.

Rename clike_langs to clink_langs for clarity

D is not a 'c-like' language, but it can link to C libraries. The same
might be true of Rust in the future and Go when we add support for it.

This contains no functionality changes.

Improve logging when dependency is anonymous

Various pieces of logging assume the dependency has a name, and aren't
grammatical if the dependency is '', so say it is anonymous instead.

Add new method: mlog.deprecation()

Instead of constructing it manually, use a helper.

Refactor getting the host system of a cross compiler

Use mesonlib.for_windows or mesonlib.for_cygwin instead of
reimplementing them.

Add CrossBuildInfo.get_host_system to shorten the repeated the code in

  with respect to Clang. LLVM and Apple Clang use
  slightly different but nowadays overlapping
  version ranges. Instead, we now just check whether
  the compiler supports the given `-std=` variant
  and try its respective fallback instead of

  which makes the code more generalisable.

phrasedml and sbml2matlab don't exist for 3.10 yet, so we need to adjust code and fail gracefully when trying to import them.

Fix wallet_send.py wallet setup to work with descriptors

Fixes the wallet setup so this test works with descriptor wallets. Also
enabled explicit descriptor and legacy wallet testing in the test
runner.

Use context managers to handle profiling

This avoids needing to remember to disable the profiler by every return statement, and reads more cleanly than using a `try` / `finally`

Add ability to construct RegressionManager with test/hook list

Standard constructor that uses discovery has been moved to the
`from_discovery` class method.

Improve __repr__ for RunningTask objects.

Displays task name, status, and current coroutine.
If the task is pending on a trigger, displays the trigger.
If the task is finished, displays the outcome.

Convert resolve() to str.translate().

New translation table class _ResolveTable provides resolve functionality
and improves performance.

This preserves current behavior of COCOTB_RESOLVE_X = RANDOM, where
all instances of the character are translated to the same value.

Create separate set of constants for operations

This is to differentiate between transaction table values and
entity operations.

Move shared static functions to utils

This allows other modules like the Celery worker to use them.

Add MonitOperator

This uses Monit's XML API and groups closely-timed Monit reloads
together.

Allow DeploymentConfig to take a KazooClient

This makes it easier to reuse the KazooClient for other things.

Reduce unnecessary "exists" watches

This allows managers to stop watches if it's clear they are no
longer needed.

Implement the datastore_v4.AllocateIds API

This allows clients to ensure that a list of entity IDs are never
re-allocated.

Simplify datastore error handling

If an error code is defined, the response body does not need to be
specified. This prevents encoding issues in cases when a response
message has required fields.

Use the EntityLock in the groomer

The allows the groomer to make index modifications under a lock
without having to create transaction IDs.

Allow Python runtime to use an external API server

If given an external api port, the Python runtime will use it to
make App Identity calls.

Attach list of groups to transaction node

This allows the transaction groomer to track down which entity
groups might have an entity lock that needs to be cleared after
the transaction is resolved.

Allow group locks to persist when commits fail

This prevents other clients from writing to a group before a large
batch is fully applied.

Simplify rollback_transaction method

This moves the protobuffer-related work to the proper layer.

Handle UpdateIndexes calls

This adds index definitions to a project's ZooKeeper node if they
aren't there yet.

Improve speed of rebalance script

This removes the call to `nodetool ring`, which can get
unreasonably slow as the amount of data in a BOP cluster increases.

It also adds a couple flags that allow the `nodetool status` call
to be skipped if the user is already sure the sanity checks will
pass.

Stop routing deleted versions

This ensures that deleted versions are absent from the HAProxy
configuration file when HAProxy is reloaded.

Move protobuffer handling to different level

Parsing the commit request and populating the response should
happen at the protobuffer interface level rather than in
DatastoreDistributed.

Add service account name field to backup form

This allows users to schedule a mapreduce-backed job with a
custom service account name for backing up to an arbitrary GCS
account.

Support the service_account_name parameter

This allows GetAccessTokenRequests to specify a custom service
account for generating an authentication token.

Allow custom service accounts for restore ops

This extends the datastore admin interface to allow custom
service accounts for restore operations.

Add support for property metadata queries

This allows clients to request a list of property names and types
for all kinds in a given namespace.

Add subdirectories for aggregates

To enable multiple aggregates in a clean way in the output directory will now contain a sub-directory for each group for which the aggregate function is called

Add RepoVersion class to make handling of many arguments easier

There are a number of arguments being passed around, nearly all of
which are duplicated between the old and new versions. Moving these
into a separate class should hopefully make it simpler to follow
what is being done.

Improve combine metadata script

1. More detailed help message
2. Helpful errors printed if assertions fail
3. Encoding of metadata origin now uses explicit "yes"/"no" values
rather than using the empty string.

Refactor sanitizer transform logic

Move logic to parse mapping of old to new column names and strip
prefixes into their own functions with tests. This refactoring
simplifies the code in the main body of the sanitizer script.

Support selecting objects under the current folder

Add a special single dot notation for filtering stories, plans and
tests under the current working directory. Update documentation
and usage messages accordingly.

Support short Fedora compose aliases in testcloud

Adds support for 'fedora' as the latest released Fedora, 'rawhide'
for the latest Rawhide plus 'fedora-X', 'f-X' and 'fX' shortcuts.

Move the Guest class from base to steps.provision

Here it makes more sense as it is related to provision classes.

Adjust the minute provision debug messages wording

Just a couple of minor cosmetic adjustments to make the messages
consistent with the rest.

Adjust the default branch handling for libraries

Detect the default branch and store it after cloning the repo.
This seems to make the implementation a bit more readable.

Implement a generic `requires` for all plugins

Add support for gathering packages required on the guest to all
supported plugins to allow easier future extension if needed.

Add a nice provisioning progress to Artemis plugin

Artemis plugin now displays the sequence of of guest states
as its provisioning progresses. This has been implemented as
a reusable primitive context manager, coupled with a small
refactoring of code taking care of indentation.

Enhance tmt.utils.retry_session with timeout support

`retry_session` is now usable as a context manager, and accepts a
timeout to honor for each HTTP request.

Current `retry_session` was overlapping with similar functionality in
`artemis` plugin, so merged both together and threw context manager in
too, because `retry_session` was used in that manner exclusively.

Convert guest implementations to use serializable container for load/save

Instead of custom load/save methods, use those based on dataclasses. We
gain type annotations, automagic conversion from/to YAML, no need for
explicit moves of fields between instances and serialized data.

Reboot has to check for boot time

Previous attempt with closing connection was not succesful as shown by
/tests/execute/reboot/reuse_provision

btime in /proc/stat is boot time in seconds since epoch and reboot()
will make sure that it has changed

Adds disk requirement for tests/full which is helps with testing

Remove unused keys parameter from wake() methods

This seems to be no longer used, and makes `wake()` more complicated
than necessary.

Unify Polarion case searching

Save and load ids to/from results.yaml.
Add constant for extra identification keys.
Raise ReportError on TC not found in Polarion.

Replace blank "type: ignore" with more specific waivers

Using mypy's error codes, waivers can target the actual erorr, leaving
space for other kind of violations to not be suppressed.

Add a helper for importing a member from a module

This primitive appeared twice already, and follows the same
scenario: import a module, then locate a member (a class, usually)
in the module, and catch possible errors along the way.

Document & correct use of class conversion methods

Recently added `{to,from}_{serialized,raw,dict}` methods for various
conversions were poorly documented, and sometimes even wrongly used.
This patch adds a short summary on when to use them, and fixes some
sub par bits around the code.

Drop various guest `wake()` methods in favor of parent class

They all do the same things anyway: instantiate a guest class, with
given data, pass parent and name down the stream. A base class can do
all of this.

Fix resuming of SOBOL generator during ax search

This is done by fixing the seed and regenerating trials already performed.

Support for dataset-specific configurations and metadata

preprocess now creates a dataset.yaml file with information about
the dataset.

Add support for relation prediction

Added a score_so method to KgeModel for this purpose and a default
implementation in RelationalScorer (which is currently used by all models).

Rename queries sp*/s*o/*po to sp_/s_o/_po

This makes them valid identifiers, which allows to use query types as
configuration keys (for example).

Define SelectionPredicateComposition

Made a new class SelectionPredicateComposition to allow use of ~,&,| with certain PredicateCompositions.  Rewrote test_filter_transform_selection_predicates to match the new syntax.

Add MPI parallelization on different MPI communicators.

This is necessary to parallelize functions that are also parallelized.

Add jobid and njobs argument to script command.

This allows to run multiple experiments from the same script in several parallel executions of YANK.

Move CLI imports into functions for speed

In order to prevent the CLI from taking long times due to importing everything, especially when the user mis-types a command for docopt to handle, import statements for the CLI functions have been moved to the actual functions instead of the module header

Improve performance of path hint generation

Avoid instantiating tons of different logic instances and just reuse the same instance by resetting its state every time it's needed.

Create and destroy C sessions inside call_module

Removes the need to always do this when using the C API. It's what the
command line app does anyway so it's not wasteful.

Hide away session management

Implement a GMTSession class to handle calling begin and end. Use it as
a global (package level) session. This way, each script/notebook uses
a single session. begin and end are no longer public API functions.

Replace the global GMTSession with 'atexit'

No need for the class or the global instance. Register 'end' with
'atexit' to make sure end is called when exiting Python.

Add 4 block attack scenarios to PV python testing

Also add the needed option -pvtest which slows down the checking
of inputs by putting a sleep time of 1 second for each input to
check.  This allows up to simulate very long to validate blocks
used in the attack scenarios.

Improve reliablility of p2p-acceptblock.py

Numerous timing issues do with the the multi-threading and also
the requestmanager. Better to no rely on sync_with_ping() and also
we have to handle getheaders requests and subsequent multi hash
getdata requests.

Add a minValue option to nonNegativeDerivative and perSecond

It works in a way similar to maxValue: when the counter wraps, instead of
producing a null value, it computes the difference assuming the counter wrapped
to minValue.

Use alternate headers for HA auth requests

When sending a "Authorization: Bearer" header to the supervisor's /auth endpoint, the header gets used to authorize the addon and then _also_ authorize against HA which fails.  This changes requests made to the /auth enpoint so they use the "X-Supervisor-Token" header to avoid the conflict.

Use library instead of ad-hoc code

This replaces `pretty_print_combos` with `json.dumps`, and
`compare_combos` with `jsoncomparison.Compare`.

Allow `MetadataFactory.fetch_http` to skip sha256

`MetadataFactory.fetch_http` must often download HTML pages, not
Updates.xml files. download.qt.io does not store checksums for these
files, so this particular function must be allowed to download these
pages without using a checksum.

Fix implementation of `helper.get_hash`

Causes `get_hash` to verify the hash length, and check that the hash can
be unhexlified properly.

Fixes the interface for `get_hash` so that the caller does not have to
run `binascii.unhexlify` or verify its output.

Add CLI option to install desktop qt automatically

This change also causes aqt to emit a warning when the option is not
turned on and the expected desktop Qt is not found.

Add test to simulate GCE instance setup

This change adds a test that sets up hosts' addressing and routing as it
is on a GCE instance, and checks that we still get connectivity between
workloads on different hosts.

Allow tests to be run on demand

With this change, a string "[test]" can be added as a comment to a pull
request by a whitelisted user to initiate testing on a pull request

Refactor to update pull requests with pending status

This commit refactors code to update the pull request with a pending
status at the earliest possible time.

Additionally, this refactor includes fixes an issue where unexpected
characters in the pull request title or body caused issues parsing
github webhook payload json

Check for available memory instead of its total amount in tests

This change prevents the python interpreter from triggering the
OOM-killer while trying to use/allocate more memory than available on
the system.

Reduce pressure on memory in stream tests

This change runs the python garbage collector before and after each
stream test.

The garbage collector is disabled in the CI since it has a significant
impact on the duration of the jobs (which are time constrained in the CI).

Fix multiline strings in schema examples

Using '\' or multiline strings results in extra whitespace, so it seems
best to use Python's automatic concatenation of adjacent strings.

Remove PDK-specific var defaults from openroad.py

We shouldn't be hardcoding tech-specific values in tool setup scripts,
so we should use the new ['pdk', 'variable'] parameter to drive these.

In order to support user overrides, we'll still drive them through the
['eda', ... 'variable'] keypath in the TCL script.

Fix RST parsing in schemagen

- Use Python standardized docstring "trim" function to preserve newlines
  and indentation in schelp strings.
- Fix schemagen parse_rst() to handle multiline text

Make _print_tcl() more robust

- Use {} to escape strings, so that we can have spaces and newlines
- Dump tuples as lists to avoid parsing
- Make sure envvar syntax gets subbed in anywhere in string

Tweak string escape approach

Use "" instead of {} to remove persistent backslashes in front of curly
braces in string.

Make tool regex set errors/warnings metrics

- "errors" and "warnings" suffix is special case
- Also update docs for relevant schema param and check_logfile()

Make regex errors/warnings additive, add reports

- Enables tools to extract additional errors/warnings from other logs
- Add logfiles under reports to reduce boilerplate, the logfiles always
  belong if regex is used

Add a spectral cutout example

Also include support for numpy arrays for band and channel, and autocorrect the band and channel values to be in ascending order

Validate `svo_fps` query parameter names locally

`SvoFpsClass.data_from_svo()` now checks the names of the query
parameters and only connects with the server if all names are valid.

Simplify setting DummyResponse data in TAP+ tests

`DummyResponse` is used in `esa/jwst` and `gaia` tests for mimicking
server responses. Now the response data can be specified by only setting
the parameters that have non-default values.

Simplify column attribute checking in `gaia` tests

The function `__check_results_column()` tested if the attributes (e.g.
description) of the columns of the query results match the expectation.
This function is now replaced with
`astropy.table.BaseColumn.attrs_equal()`, and the comparison data is now
provided by a `pytest` fixture.

Reduce duplication in setting up `gaia` tests

The new module level fixtures allowed removing setup code from many
tests.

Remove `TestTap` class from `gaia` tests

Grouping the tests together in a test class served no purpose and
eliminating the class removed a level of indentation.

Remove `utils.tap.conn.TapConn.url_encode()`

The removed method simply called the standard library
`urllib.parse.urlencode()`.

Remove an utility function for reading test data

`astroquery.utils.tap.xmlparser.utils.read_file_content()` has been
replaced with the standard library `pathlib.Path.read_text()`.
Furthermore, in the modules where multiple test functions previously
used `read_file_content()` to read the data files, they are now read
once at the module level instead.
